channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: Could your protein powder cost more? The US-Canada trade war is putting whey at risk
item.description: The US-Canada trade war is reaching the protein aisle, with whey facing tariffs and import restrictions. Canadian manufacturers warn of higher costs and supply problems, while US consumers could also feel the impact.

item.title: Bank employees worked on Sunday but Monday strike deferred; change in plan triggers meme fest online
item.description: Bank employees worked on Sunday ahead of a planned three-day strike, but the action was deferred after late-night talks between IBA and UFBU. The sudden change left social media users turning the unexpected development into a meme fest.&nbsp;

item.title: Bank strike on 28, 29, 30 September deferred; salaried individuals to get money in account as usual?
item.description: The bank strike originally planned for 28-30 September has been deferred. Will your salary reach the account as usual?

item.title: Parvesh Verma slap row: What to know about Tilak Nagar road inspection incident in Delhi as AAP protests — 5 points
item.description: A political controversy erupted in Delhi after a video surfaced showing PWD Minister Parvesh Verma allegedly slapping a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar. The opposition AAP demanded action against Verma, while he defended his actions, claiming provocation from AAP supporters.

item.title: 3-day bank strike has been deferred: Check UFBU's complete statement; decision on Saturdays as holidays, and more
item.description: 3-day bank strike has been deferred, UFBU has confirmed in a statement.

item.title: FM Sitharaman to visit Qatar from 27-29 September, attend AIIB annual meeting
item.description: India is a founding member of AIIB and among its largest shareholders, giving it a significant role in the institution's governance.

item.title: IndiGo flight suffers tail strike while landing in Bengaluru amid gusty weather conditions
item.description: An IndiGoflight from Guwahati to Bengaluru suffered a tail strike during its second landing approach at Kempegowda International Airport amid gusty weather. All passengers and crews were reported safe after the aircradft landed.&nbsp;

item.title: Lovely Professional University protest turns violent: Protesters clash with police, stones pelted over 'rape' case
item.description: Police said a rape case has been registered against an unknown person on a complaint by the students, and an SIT has been formed to investigate the matter.

item.title: 3-day bank strike: Will your September salary be delayed? Here’s all you need to know
item.description: Ahead of a bank strike from September 28-30, public sector banks operated on September 27. While UPI and online services will function, cash transactions may be delayed.

item.title: Daylight Saving Time 2026: Why Americans will get an extra hour on November 1 after Halloween
item.description: Clocks across most of the US will move back by one hour on 1 November 2026, ending daylight saving time. The change comes just after Halloween and gives many people an extra hour overnight as standard time returns.

item.title: Bengaluru traffic gets worse? Cars queue up inside society as users say ‘never come out ever’
item.description: The woman initially filmed the traffic on the road from her room before turning the camera towards the residential complex. The footage appeared to show vehicles moving slowly towards the society's exit.

item.title: Your favourite grocery snacks may vanish in 2026 — here’s why Pepsi and major brands are cutting products
item.description: Several familiar snacks and drinks are disappearing from US grocery shelves in 2026 as major food companies streamline their ranges, respond to changing demand and focus on products they see as stronger sellers.

item.title: New York and Northeast Facing Another Day of Wild Weather
item.description: New Yorkers can expect rain and high winds through Monday as a powerful nor’easter that caused moderate flooding in Manhattan’s Battery continues to pound the area, knocking out power to thousands and grounding hundreds of flights.

item.title: ‘No UPI Day’ on October 2? Mobile retailers protest proposed 0.4% MDR on payments
item.description: AIMRA has called for merchant UPI payments to continue under the existing zero-MDR structure. AIMRA Vice President and Delhi-NCR President Tarvinder Singh said the association had chosen October 2 for the protest to draw attention to the concerns of mobile retailers.

item.title: Heavy rain likely in parts of north India, northeast and south over next week
item.description: The IMD has forecast widespread rain in parts of India through early October, even as the southwest monsoon continues to withdraw from the northwest.

item.title: Tamil Nadu government withdraws RTI exemption for Law and Order Department amid criticism
item.description: The government had initially issued the exemption under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act, classifying the Public (Law and Order) Department as an Intelligence and Security Organisation.

item.title: PM calls on citizens to participate in Census 2027
item.description: The government has introduced self-enumeration, allowing citizens to submit household details online in 16 languages.

item.title: Bihar’s ₹21,000 crore mineral reserves may generate over ₹5,000 crore annual revenue, says report
item.description: Bihar aims to revitalise its mineral economy by harnessing new resources worth over ₹21,000 crore. Geological surveys have reportedly identified valuable minerals like glauconite and gold, but challenges remain in transitioning to commercial production.&nbsp;

item.title: Who is Priyanka Saxena? After 10 years in IAF, she lost her fighter pilot husband; SC backs her return
item.description: Priyanka Saxena joined the Indian Air Force at the Air Force Academy in Hyderabad in January 2002 and received her commission on 20 December 2003.

item.title: Russian Strikes Kill Four in Ukraine, Damage Kyiv Data Center
item.description: Russia’s overnight airstrikes killed at least four people across Ukraine and hit a data center in Kyiv, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

item.title: Consumer drags PVR Cinemas to court after ads play for 17 minutes before movie: Movie chain must now pay ₹75,000
item.description: PVR INOX played ads for 17 minutes before a movie. The consumer turned out to be an advocate. Now, the chain must pay ₹75,000 in fine.

item.title: PM Modi's Mann Ki Baat Top Quotes: From surgical strike to amla, Ashok Singhal and ‘most beautiful tribute to Bapu’
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke on a host of issues in the latest edition of Mann Ki Baat — from recalling the 2016 surgical strike to highlighting Amla-based rural enterprise and nutrition initiatives in Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh. Here are the top quotes from PM Modi's Mann ki Baat.

item.title: Brics can serve as a platform for talks, cooperation, and reaching consensus: Iranian ambassador Fathali
item.description: The New Delhi Declaration at the 18th Brics Summit was important because it stressed national sovereignty, territorial integrity and international law, while voicing concern over attacks on nuclear facilities, civilians and the humanitarian situation in Gaza, says Iran’s ambassador to India.

item.title: Mint Explainer | Why a super-charged El Niño is a postcard from our future
item.description: This year’s El Niño will be a ‘postcard from our future’ bringing temperatures that climate change is projected to deliver 20 years into the future, warned the Climate Impact Lab at the University of Chicago.

item.title: US-Iran war: Mojtaba Khamenei 'pulled from rubble' after strikes — New claim after Trump says Supreme leader ‘not dead’
item.description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei was rushed to a Tehran hospital after a US-Israel strike in the early days of the war, only to be “pulled from the rubble” again after the US and Israel bombed the medical centre, an Iranian cleric said this week.

item.title: Mint explainer: what has changed in the new HAM highway contract?
item.description: MoRTH’s new HAM framework links construction payments to certified physical progress, while adding financing support, tighter monitoring, risk-sharing and road-safety requirements.

item.title: Who is Petal Gahlot? First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, who schooled Pak PM Shehbaz Sharif at UNGA
item.description: Petal Gahlot, First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, is in the spotlight after delivering India’s Right of Reply to Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif. Here’s a look at her education, diplomatic career and previous UNGA interventions.

item.title: World Tourism Day 2026 special: These 5 locations became fan pilgrimage after iconic movies - Full details here
item.description: As the travel industry embraces “set-jetting,” the trend of travelling to locations featured in movies and TV shows, some spots have evolved into permanent shrines for die-hard fans.

item.title: Students protest at Punjab's LPU, rape allegation sparks outrage — What we know so far
item.description: Videos circulating on social media showed students at LPU damaging window panes and flower pots, and even setting some objects on fire. A heavy police force has been deployed at the university, with police stating that the situation is now under control.

item.title: Air India AI 171 crash: FIP writes to Aviation Minister, seeks inclusion of technical submissions in AAIB's report
item.description: The Federation of Indian Pilots has urged the Civil Aviation Ministry to ensure its technical inputs are considered before the AAIB finalises its AI171 crash probe, citing discrepancies between the preliminary report and simulator assessments.

item.title: Early winter in Delhi? Minimum temperature settles below season's normal; more rain likely on Sunday
item.description: The minimum temperature settled below the season's average at 21 degrees Celsius on Sunday. The weather department has predicted a cloudy sky with the maximum temperature expected to touch 31 degrees Celsius.

item.title: Russia, other countries back India's bid for permanent seat at UNSC, Lavrov opposes additional seats to Western nations
item.description: Russia has backed India's bid for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council, while opposing additional seats for Western countries. Several other nations, including Mauritius and members of the G4, have also supported India's candidacy and called for UNSC reforms.

item.title: Bengaluru techie's reality check on ₹2 crore flats goes viral — ‘Gen Z getting humbled by housing prices’
item.description: The techie noted that he leads a frugal lifestyle and had savings, but even with significant savings, a decent home in a gated community remains out of reach.

item.title: One dead, hundreds of flights cancelled, power lines hit as 'Nor'easter' storm batters parts of US: What we know so far
item.description: New York, Boston and Philadelphia were all in the firing line of the “Nor'easter” — so labeled for its northeasterly winds — as authorities warned of potential major flooding and road closures, AFP reported.

item.title: Google's birthday: Why the September 27 celebration doesn't match its official September 4 incorporation date
item.description: Google Doodle marked the tech giant's 28th birthday with rare 1997 beta logo throwback. Check history, significance and more about September 27 celebrations…
